strategies.name: Baseline Three-Stage All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Three sequential xm.all_reduce calls with intermediate local scaling operations (clone, multiply, divide) between them. 3 collective dispatches with full W*S payload each time. Represents the straightforward faithful translation with no optimization—highest dispatch count but simplest correctness reasoning.

strategies.name: Fused Local-Ops Between Collectives
strategies.desc: Same three all_reduce calls but eliminate clone() operations by carefully reusing buffers and fusing all element-wise operations (scale, divide) into single in-place loops per stage. Still 3 collective dispatches but reduces local memory allocations and potentially enables better JIT fusion of scalar ops, trading code clarity for memory pressure.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decompose each all_reduce into reduce_scatter (producing W*S/W per rank) followed by all_gather, yielding 6 collective dispatches total. Smaller intermediate payloads (S per rank instead of W*S) reduce per-dispatch bandwidth cost; the local scaling operations now apply to S-sized chunks, potentially improving cache locality at the cost of doubled collective count.

strategies.name: Single All-Reduce with Stacked Metadata
strategies.desc: Concatenate the three logical "versions" of the data into a single 3*W*S tensor, perform one all_reduce, then use views/slicing to apply the appropriate per-shard scales to each of the three sections and fold results back. 1 collective dispatch with 3x payload, trading bandwidth for latency—beneficial if dispatch overhead dominates and network can sustain larger messages.

strategies.name: Pipelined Ring-Based Custom Collective
strategies.desc:
Replace all_reduce primitives with explicit send/recv ring passes, interleaving communication of different stages' chunks so that while stage-k data travels, stage-(k+1) local computation proceeds on already-arrived chunks. Increases total collective operations but overlaps communication with computation, beneficial when local ops are non-trivial and network is bandwidth-bound rather than latency-bound.

def r1_fold_s256_fn(x, rank, world_size, num_devices,
                 cores_per_device, xm, torch, num_nodes=1):
    S = 256
    W = world_size
    dtype = x.dtype
    
    # Precompute scale factors as a tensor for vectorized operations
    a = torch.tensor([1.0 + 0.5 * (r % 3) for r in range(W)], 
                     dtype=dtype, device=x.device)
    
    # Repeat each scale factor S times to match tensor shape
    scale_vector = a.repeat_interleave(S)
    
    # Stage 1: all_reduce
    s1 = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, x)
    
    # Vectorized operation: scale and divide
    s1 = (scale_vector / W) * s1
    
    # Stage 2: all_reduce
    s2 = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, s1)
    
    # Vectorized operation: divide by scale factor and world size
    # Equivalent to s2 / (a[r] * W) for each segment, then multiply by a[r]
    # This simplifies to s2 / W
    s2 = s2 / W
    
    # Stage 3: all_reduce
    out = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, s2)
    
    return out
